stem:
Kartik's teacher says Class 7 science is more than a list of facts to memorise. Kartik compares four study habits for the chapter on the ever-evolving world of science.

Which habit treats science as a process of curiosity, questioning, experimenting, and looking for patterns?

options.text: He notices that wet footprints dry at different speeds on tile and mat, asks why, and plans a small timed test.
He decides that learning any facts means he is not thinking scientifically at all.
He says testing why a puddle dries outside school cannot count as science.
He copies a textbook page headed Experiment word for word and calls that inquiry.

teacher.key_rationale: Science here is an active process: curiosity, questions, experiments, and patterns. Rejecting all fact learning omits balance; excluding outdoor puddle tests narrows scope; copying an Experiment heading captures a surface feature.
